children.text: What young children learn with us

Our day follows a play-based curriculum built on Experience Early Learning. Each week has a theme, and children explore it through stories, songs, art, building, pretend play and simple science. A developmental continuum helps us see what each child can do and what to work on next, so your child is never pushed too fast or held back.

Every day starts with circle time: we go over the calendar and the weather, practice letters and numbers, and talk about the day ahead. A picture schedule on the classroom wall helps younger children know what comes next, which makes the day calmer for everyone.

excerpt: Toddler care and kindergarten readiness for ages 2.5 to 5, open Monday to Saturday at our licensed Vineland center.

faqs.answer: Children can start at 2½ years old. We care for toddlers and young children up to 5, and 4 and 5-year-olds work on kindergarten readiness. School-age children up to 13 join our before and after school care.
faqs.question: What age can my child start at Uriah?

faqs.answer: No. Many of our 2½ and 3-year-olds are still learning. We work on potty training together with you, using the same routine at home and at the center.
faqs.question: Does my child need to be potty trained?

faqs.answer: We use a play-based curriculum built on Experience Early Learning, with weekly themes and a developmental continuum of skills in language, math, science, art and social skills.
faqs.question: What curriculum do you use?

faqs.answer: We accept NJ childcare subsidy (CCAP) for families who qualify. Call us and we will walk you through the steps with the Cumberland County agency.
faqs.question: Is care for young children covered by CCAP?
